name: A record with nothing on it is a failed read, not an applicant already done
request: A record with nothing on it is a failed read, not an applicant already done
result: Reported: 'even if I click the extension to start again it does not scroll the profile.' The list pass built its skip index with createListedIndex - createCollectedIndex(..., anyRecord: true), 'do I already HAVE them' - which counts a record with nothing on it as done. Every path that fails on an applicant still writes the row's own name as a floor so nobody is lost, so the applicants a broken run FAILED on were exactly the ones the next run retired in bulk without opening, and no number of button presses could reach them. createListedIndex existed for one reason - that pass wrote name-only records - and that reason evaporated when it started opening each applicant and writing a full record. Removed, with the anyRecord flag and the { listed } parameter on loadCollectedIndex; both commands now ask isCollectedApplicant, which wants one substantive field, so a complete read is skipped and a thin one is tried again. The worker still sends every stored entry with the verdict beside it rather than filtering on it - the index applies the verdict, the worker only reports - so the payload is unchanged. The test that asserted the two indexes stay distinguishable is replaced by one asserting a floor-name record is never skipped, judged both from the worker's verdict and from the record itself.
